children: New Jersey Resources (
) today announced that three of its long-time leaders have been named officers at NJR’s subsidiary businesses.
Kevin Dixon
promoted to Vice President-Commercial, Business Development and Project Execution at NJR’s Storage and Transportation (S&T) business.
Brian Emerson
promoted to Vice President-Field Operations at New Jersey Natural Gas (NJNG).
Garrett Lerner
promoted to Vice President-Business Development and Finance at NJR Clean Energy Ventures (CEV).
These changes are effective January 1, 2027.

“Kevin, Brian and Garrett are respected leaders at our company that have supported our record of safe, reliable service, business growth and innovation,” said Steve Westhoven, President and CEO of New Jersey Resources. “With their extensive expertise and market knowledge, I am confident they will be effective members of NJR’s leadership team and play an integral role in delivering continued performance for our company, customers and shareowners.”

Mr. Dixon was named Director-Marketing and Business Development for NJR Energy Services, NJR’s natural gas marketing business, in 2016. He joined S&T in 2019, where he served as Managing Director-Midstream and in 2023, he was appointed Managing Director-Commercial, Business Development and Project Execution. Earlier in his career, he worked at Devon Energy Corporation, Williams Midstream and held several leadership positions at Columbia Pipeline Group, now TC Energy.

As Vice President-Commercial, Business Development and Project Execution, Mr. Dixon will be responsible for setting the vision and executing on the strategy and priorities for S&T’s Commercial operations, including leading commercial development and identifying pipeline and storage investment opportunities that drive growth.

Mr. Emerson joined NJNG in 1993 and has more than three decades of utility experience, including serving as a First Responder, Distribution Supervisor and most recently Managing Director of Field Operations. He also previously served as Manager of Labor and Employee Relations.

In his new role, Mr. Emerson will be responsible for establishing the strategic direction and priorities for NJNG’s field operations, including providing for the safe, reliable operations and maintenance of the utility’s natural gas distribution facilities, ensuring workforce readiness and setting the standard for safety and operational excellence.

Mr. Lerner began his career at NJR in 2014 as a Transportation Analyst at NJR Energy Services. He joined CEV in 2018, where he served in several leadership positions, including Manager-Solar Business Development, Director-Development and Finance and most recently as Managing Director-Development and Finance.

In his new role as CEV’s Vice President-Business Development and Finance, Mr. Lerner will lead the development and execution of investment strategies for renewable energy projects and portfolio opportunities. He will also be responsible for identifying and implementing strategies to extract added value from CEV’s operational asset base.

“Together, Kevin, Brian and Garrett bring more than 50 years of energy experience and expertise to their new roles,” Westhoven said. “As the newest members of NJR’s executive team, they will be a key part of developing and advancing NJR’s long-term growth strategy.”
About New Jersey Resources:
New Jersey Resources
) is a diversified energy infrastructure and energy services company headquartered in Wall, New Jersey.
NJR is composed of five primary businesses:
New Jersey Natural Gas,
NJR’s principal subsidiary,
operates and maintains natural gas transportation and distribution infrastructure to serve customers in New Jersey’s Monmouth, Ocean, Morris, Middlesex, Sussex and Burlington counties.
NJR Clean Energy Ventures
invests in, owns and operates solar projects, providing customers with low-carbon solutions.
NJR Energy Services
manages a diversified portfolio of natural gas transportation and storage assets and provides physical natural gas services and customized energy solutions to its customers across North America.
Storage and Transportation

serves customers from local distributors and producers to electric generators and wholesale marketers through its ownership of Leaf River and the Adelphia Gateway Pipeline, as well as our 50% equity ownership in the Steckman Ridge natural gas storage facility.
Home Services
provides service contracts as well as heating, central air conditioning, water heaters, standby generators and other indoor and outdoor comfort products to residential homes throughout New Jersey.

NJR and its almost 1,400 employees are committed to helping customers save energy and money by promoting conservation and encouraging efficiency through Conserve to Preserve® and initiatives such as SAVEGREEN®.
